sources.cite: Microsoft Learn, Overview of Service Bus dead-letter queues
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Quoted: the DLQ holds 'messages that can't be delivered to any receiver, or messages that couldn't be processed'; path <queue path>/$deadletterqueue; 'There's no automatic cleanup of the DLQ. Messages remain in the DLQ until you explicitly retrieve them'; default maximum delivery count 10, after which the reason is MaxDeliveryCountExceeded; resubmit with Service Bus Explorer, which lets you 'peek messages in the dead-letter queue, edit their content or properties if needed, and resend them'. Receive-resend-then-complete is the fetch's own sketch, not the page's.

brief.situation: You are the developer on call at Corvin Garden Supply. Last night's release of the order-processing Function had a bug: it rejected any order with a gift message. Each such message failed ten times and went to the dead-letter queue of the Service Bus queue orders. The bug was fixed and redeployed at 07:20. The warehouse's 09:00 picking wave needs every paid order in the system.
handover: The fixed function version is 2026.11.17.2; its tests include gift-message orders now.
Orders are idempotent by order ID in the order database.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the orders queue, its dead-letter queue and the function that processes orders.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why orders were dead-lettered, how you got them processed, and how this is caught earlier.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: Last night's function release rejected orders with a gift message; each failed ten deliveries and was dead-lettered with MaxDeliveryCountExceeded. Every sample has a gift message.

parts.label: Processed
parts.modelAnswer: Confirmed version 2026.11.17.2 processes a gift-message order and that writes are idempotent, then resubmitted all 3,214 in batches, completing each dead-letter message only after its resend. Purging would have deleted them.

parts.label: Earlier
parts.modelAnswer: An alert fires when the dead-letter count passes 10, and the release tests include optional fields like gift messages.

scoring.modelReasoning: Every dead-lettered message failed on delivery count and carries a gift message, which last night's bug rejected; the fixed version processes such an order and writes are idempotent. Resubmit the messages in batches, completing each dead-letter copy only after its resend, and check the database. Purging deletes paid orders; restarting the function does nothing because dead-lettered messages are never redelivered on their own. Alert on the DLQ count.
